scope: Internal default/parallel process dispatcher, worker replacement and retries
processControls: Four real child workers and worker fixture reuse across successful groups
Fresh process after failure; stable slot and monotonic worker index
BeforeAll descendant skip receipts and next retry numbers
Original results preserved across exit and blocked-callback watchdog
Normal worker teardown errors fail the suite without rewriting passed tests
Fatal receipt after final done fails the run
TERM-resistant same-group descendant killed after leader exit
Observer rejection drains afterAll hooks before worker fixtures and preserves all errors
retainedCorrections: Review found dropped idle worker failures, premature cancellation of process-group escalation, skipped suite cleanup after observer rejection, and compatible-job preference reordering the queue. Final focused controls and review cover the corrections.

The first application attempt failed before browser allocation because its adapter has asynchronous dependencies. The private process module now awaits adapter import before entering synchronous test collection.
limitations: Internal Unix process runner only; public config/CLI/reporter/artifact integration, serial retries and compatible deadlines remain open.
Watchdog termination is a liveness mechanism, not Playwright per-test timeout semantics or proof of all detached descendant cleanup.
Browser suites cover passing execution at one/four workers; process crash/watchdog tests here use controlled fixtures without browsers.
Collection comparison covers test identity, callback source, expected status and group partitions, not equality of every hook closure or fixture value across processes.
The 2x goal, final resource admission, release and public runner promotion remain open.
